# Directed graph preservation — facts

> Source-anchored units about Directed graph preservation: 16 across 6 sources. Each line ends in the URL and anchor it came from; `keywords:` names the lexicon terms that matched.

<!-- generated by llms-concept-abstractor v1.4.1 · generated 2026-11-08 · 16 units · 6 sources · rights: quote -->

## How it works

- [statement] Bennett, Cucuringu and Reinert describe significance thresholding when constructing a lead-lag network: an edge is retained only when the associated lead-lag metric is sufficiently large. A direction-preserving encoding therefore addresses a different stage from deciding which inferred edges to retain. (low confidence) — https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10994-022-06250-4 · keywords: Directed graph preservation

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] Symmetrizing a directed adjacency matrix loses edge orientation. For a lead-lag graph, retaining that symmetrized matrix alone therefore cannot preserve which variable leads which; this application is a methodological inference from the graph representations. (high confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9425115/ · keywords: Directed graph preservation · also: https://arxiv.org/html/2411.15527v2
- [statement] The QuaterGCN authors target unequal antiparallel edge pairs without collapsing them into one edge. The later Haar-Laplacian paper independently identifies a failure of sign-magnetic encoding for reciprocal edges. Thus, support for signed directed inputs alone is insufficient evidence of full graph preservation. (high confidence) — https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.17361 · keywords: Directed graph preservation · also: https://arxiv.org/html/2411.15527v2
- [statement] Bennett, Cucuringu and Reinert report low overall persistence and year-to-year instability in their empirical US-equity lead-lag structure. This is a scope warning for carrying an inferred graph across time; it does not measure five-minute SOL graph stability. (low confidence) — https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10994-022-06250-4 · keywords: Directed graph preservation

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] The Deep Fusion seed paper explicitly symmetrizes its directed adjacency matrix to use node embeddings. This is a material loss for directional lead–lag interpretation: Bennett, Cucuringu and Reinert explain that naive symmetrization-based clustering uses edge density rather than edge direction. (medium confidence) — https://arxiv.org/pdf/2201.02040 · keywords: Directed graph preservation · also: https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10994-022-06250-4
- [statement] MSGNN supplies a directly relevant application: its authors introduce datasets built from financial time-series lead-lag relationships alongside a spectral architecture for signed directed graphs. This establishes application relevance, rather than proving that any inferred edge is causal. (low confidence) — https://proceedings.mlr.press/v198/he22c.html · keywords: Directed graph preservation
- [statement] The Haar-Laplacian construction combines symmetric and skew-symmetric adjacency parts into a Hermitian encoding; adding those parts reconstructs the original adjacency. Its stated graph setup excludes self-loops. For a preservation audit, this supplies a concrete reversible construction within those assumptions, rather than a claim about every graph format or normalization. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2411.15527v2 · keywords: Directed graph preservation
- [statement] Novelli and colleagues evaluate inferred directed networks using synthetic linear and nonlinear dynamics. They report that varying the significance threshold changes the precision-recall tradeoff, with more favorable tradeoffs for longer time series. This concerns inference reliability, separately from whether a graph representation retains direction. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6663300/ · keywords: Directed graph preservation

## Facts and statements

- [statement] MagNet encodes direction in complex phase, but setting its charge parameter q to zero reduces it to adjacency symmetrization; using a magnetic operator alone therefore does not ensure that direction is retained. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9425115/ · keywords: Directed graph preservation
- [statement] The SigMaNet authors introduce a parameter-free Sign-Magnetic Laplacian for directed graphs whose weights can have either sign and unrestricted magnitude. This is an attributed design claim, not a guarantee for every directed topology. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.13459 · keywords: Directed graph preservation
- [statement] The QuaterGCN authors identify unequal-weight antiparallel edge pairs as a preservation requirement: their Quaternionic Laplacian represents those pairs without reducing them to one directed or undirected edge. Their claim scopes the broader idea that encoding edge direction necessarily preserves the whole weighted graph. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.17361 · keywords: Directed graph preservation
- [statement] Fitch constructs an undirected symmetrization with the same pairwise effective resistances as its directed input. This is a specific metric-preservation guarantee; it does not state that the undirected output retains each edge orientation. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/abs/1802.09829 · keywords: Directed graph preservation
- [statement] NetworkX issue 8560 proposes magnetic_laplacian_matrix and magnetic_laplacian_spectrum for directed spectral analysis. The issue is implementation-discussion evidence; it does not establish that either function shipped in a release. (low confidence) — https://github.com/networkx/networkx/issues/8560 · keywords: Directed graph preservation
- [statement] MagNet encodes directional information in complex phase, while entry magnitudes encode undirected geometry. Encoding direction is a representation property and should be checked separately from preserving all reciprocal edge weights. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9425115/ · keywords: Directed graph preservation · also: https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.17361
- [statement] The SigMaNet authors describe a parameter-free sign-magnetic Laplacian for directed and undirected graphs with unrestricted weight sign and magnitude, and report that its direction encoding avoids a weight-magnitude problem of other Laplacians. This does not establish preservation of every reciprocal weight pair. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.13459 · keywords: Directed graph preservation
- [statement] The cited NetworkX documentation snapshot states that converting a directed graph to an undirected graph can collapse differing reciprocal edge data to one arbitrarily chosen value. This supports the conclusion that the conversion alone does not preserve both directional weights; it does not establish behavior for every historical package release. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-08) — https://networkx.org/documentation/stable/reference/classes/generated/networkx.DiGraph.to_undirected.html · keywords: Directed graph preservation
